question: Why can a black-and-white print that was properly fixed still turn yellow years later?
answer: Because the fixer was not washed out. Fibre-based paper soaks up thiosulphate, the fixing agent, and holds it in its fibres. Left there, it slowly breaks down and attacks the silver image, forming yellow-brown silver sulphide, first in the highlights. Hence long washes. Stains can surface decades after a print looked perfect.
move: Cleaning up after a process is part of the process.
ask: Which of my jobs is not really finished until I have done the cleanup that follows?
source: Stroebel et al., Basic Photographic Materials, 2000
reference: Leslie Stroebel, John Compton, Ira Current & Richard Zakia, Basic Photographic Materials and Processes, 2nd edition, Focal Press, 2000
